bug_semantics: A project-scoped caller who is authorized to PATCH a volume target but is not authorized by baremetal:volume:view_target_properties can modify an unrelated allowed field and receive the complete updated VolumeTarget in the HTTP 200 response. The PATCH path serializes new_target with convert_with_links() without applying the view-target-properties redaction used by GET/list, so properties that can hold iSCSI connection details and credentials are disclosed. POST has the same unredacted serialization shape, but the requester supplied those values; the security-relevant information gain identified by the bundle is PATCH, where an otherwise-authorized edit reveals pre-existing secrets.
flaw_origin: Commit e870bd34d0ccacbaef7f4e4def2535eb28f822b9 created the exploitable authorization split. It expanded baremetal:volume:update to system and project scopes (including owner members/lessee admins), introduced the stricter baremetal:volume:view_target_properties policy, and added that policy's redaction to GET/list only. It left PATCH returning convert_with_links(new_target) without the new redaction check. The unredacted PATCH response itself originated with the volume-target API in c380e05dbf84079b01fb3b0ea099ef9b293b9b3d and was mechanically rewritten by 000bc72cc29b8637df496f2e6768281606a27058, but neither is the security BIC: before e870bd34 the update endpoint was system-scoped and there was no distinct lower privilege that could update while being denied target properties.
ai_marker: absent — the raw BIC commit object names human author and committer Julia Kreger <juliaashleykreger@gmail.com>; its message has only Change-Id: I898310b515195b7065a3b1c7998ef3f29f5e8747 and contains no Co-Authored-By, Assisted-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: First-party advisory evidence: OSSA-2026-023 (https://security.openstack.org/ossa/OSSA-2026-023.html) says authenticated POST/PATCH callers to /v1/volume/targets could receive sensitive properties such as iSCSI credentials, lists affected package ranges >=17.0.0 <29.0.6, >=30.0.0 <32.0.2, >=33.0.0 <35.0.2, and >=36.0.0 <37.0.1, and notes that the endpoint existed from 9.0.0 but became a privilege escalation only after 17.0.0 introduced project-scoped owner/lessee access. Launchpad bug 2155049 further distinguishes the meaningful PATCH case: editing an unrelated field must not reveal existing secrets, whereas POST returns values the caller supplied.

BIC code evidence: git show e870bd34d0ccacbaef7f4e4def2535eb28f822b9 shows ironic/common/policy.py:1431-1459 changing baremetal:volume:update to SYSTEM_OR_OWNER_MEMBER_AND_LESSEE_ADMIN with system/project scopes and adding the separate TARGET_PROPERTIES_READER-backed baremetal:volume:view_target_properties rule. In ironic/api/controllers/v1/volume_target.py:247-260 the same commit checks that new view policy and redacts GET, but PATCH at lines 348-350 checks only baremetal:volume:update and lines 404-407 directly serialize and return new_target without a view-properties check. POST lines 292-317 likewise has no redaction, but does not create the bundle's pre-existing-secret information gain.

History decomposition evidence: git log -L 346,407:ironic/api/controllers/v1/volume_target.py at the BIC traces the response serialization back through the plain-JSON refactor 000bc72cc29b8637df496f2e6768281606a27058 to endpoint creation c380e05dbf84079b01fb3b0ea099ef9b293b9b3d. git log -L 123,134 on the pre-fix tree identifies e870bd34d0ccacbaef7f4e4def2535eb28f822b9 as the commit that first introduced _redact_target_properties. This is not a squash to decompose: git cat-file commit shows one parent and a normal Gerrit Change-Id; the causal unit is the single RBAC commit that simultaneously created the split privilege and omitted enforcement on the write-response path.

Immediate-parent absence: git rev-parse e870bd34^ resolves e9dfe5ddaad7324d8d89fef0661f41f18542028f. Direct parent-tree git grep finds no view_target_properties symbol. Parent ironic/common/policy.py:1390-1398 defines baremetal:volume:update as check_str=SYSTEM_MEMBER with scope_types=['system'] only. Therefore the parent retained an unredacted response but did not permit the project-scoped update-without-view privilege combination; the vulnerable authorization differential is absent in the immediate parent.

Affected-version boundary: git merge-base --is-ancestor e870bd34d0ccacbaef7f4e4def2535eb28f822b9 17.0.0 succeeds, while the same check against 16.0.5 fails. This places the BIC in the first affected 17.0.0 line and excludes the final 16.0 maintenance tag, matching the OSSA explanation of why the older endpoint code did not yet constitute this privilege escalation.

Fix evidence: advisory-linked master commit dd2df520fe0ae019cb247a8295542abc2d4b46dd changes ironic/api/controllers/v1/volume_target.py so PATCH checks baremetal:volume:view_target_properties and calls _redact_target_properties before convert_with_links; it also replaces generic sanitize_dict use with target_sanitize, which masks password-like values in properties across serialization paths. The commit's Assisted-By: Claude Opus 4.6 trailer is on the 2026 fix only and is excluded from BIC attribution by the protocol.

Patched-release cross-check: stable/2025.1 backport 49bff4c09acfdf195f40f911236b9ac5c6def3c5 is an ancestor of tag 29.0.6 and is not an ancestor of 29.0.5, directly confirming one advisory first-patched boundary. The master fix dd2df520fe0ae019cb247a8295542abc2d4b46dd is an ancestor of the repository's 37.0.0 tag, whose annotated metadata says meta:pypi: no; the advisory therefore names 37.0.1 as the first patched pip package version even though the unpublished 37.0.0 code tag already contains the fix. The validated clone does not yet contain a 37.0.1 tag, but the public fixing commit and an independently tagged maintained-branch patched boundary are present and verified.

BIC-only AI inspection: numactl-prefixed git cat-file commit e870bd34d0ccacbaef7f4e4def2535eb28f822b9 reports tree b92287d93bd5f4eb3f7e4295a59f63a8d1cc0eb5, sole parent e9dfe5ddaad7324d8d89fef0661f41f18542028f, author/committer Julia Kreger, the project-scoped RBAC message, and only a Gerrit Change-Id trailer. No commit-object AI signal exists on the BIC.
reasoning: The lifecycle has two distinct stages. The volume-target PATCH response was introduced in Ironic's 9.0-era endpoint work and continued returning the complete updated object, but its authorization was system-scoped, so that response shape alone did not let a caller with update permission cross a separate target-secret visibility boundary. The smallest commit that made the advisory's exploit real is e870bd34: it opened update operations to project-scoped owner/lessee roles and, in the same commit, defined a narrower policy for viewing target properties. It correctly enforced that new policy on GET/list yet omitted it from PATCH, leaving a lower-privileged updater able to recover pre-existing properties by changing another field. The immediate parent has neither the view-properties policy nor project-scoped volume update, directly proving absence. The BIC is in 17.0.0 but not 16.0.5, which exactly matches the advisory's security boundary. dd2df520 and its backports close both layers by enforcing PATCH redaction and masking password-like property values during serialization; the 29.0.6/29.0.5 ancestry checks confirm a concrete patched boundary. Finally, the raw e870bd34 commit object is human-authored/committed and has no AI marker. Claude attribution exists only on the later fix and cannot attribute the BIC, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
